the thermal transformation of zeolite A into monoclinic barium aluminosilicate (BaO⋅6Al2O3⋅6SiO2) may be accomplished at temperatures far lower than those required to obtain the same transformation starting from zeolitic X, and that the presence of Li may accelerate the transformation of zeolites into the monoclinic calsian phase.
the thermal transformation of zeolites into celsian is possible and that the presence of lithium is beneficial in the formation of the final product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of celsian from Ba-exchanged precursors of the A and X zeotypes.
the synthesis of a new ceramic composite material based on a celsian matrix and zeolite A crystals dispersed throughout the celsian.
the synthesis of a new family of materials, the so-called celsian zeolite, which is characterized by the presence of a zeolitic framework and by the presence of the BaAl2Si2O8 celsian phase.

the thermal transformation of Ba-exchange A and X zeols into monoclinic BaAl2Si2O8 is possible by using a suitable thermal treatment, which depends on the nature of the precursor zeolite, on the nature and concentration of the exchangeable cation, and on the heating rate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal transformation of zeolite X into celsian is a more complicated process than the thermal transformation of Ba-exchaged zeolite A into celsian.

the thermal transformations of zeolites into celsian may occur at temperatures as low as 900°C in a very short time (6 h) in the presence of both Li and Ba, and that the use of zeolite A is advantageous with respect to that of zeolite X.

zeolite A may be considered an effective precursor to prepare monoclinic celsius at temperatures far below the temperatures required to obtain the same product from zeolite Na-X.
